reference_summary: JPMorgan made JPM Coin, a digital token representing U.S. dollar deposits at the bank, available to institutional clients on Ethereum, expanding beyond Coinbase's Base network. The bank said the move gives large clients more ways to transfer money, pay for trades and support other digital financial assets. JPMorgan chose Ethereum because of the funds available for trading there and its existing use by institutional clients.

title: Strategy's price chart is about to flash a major bullish signal weeks after bitcoin did

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here, if you haven't already.
Weeks after bitcoin’s (BTC) price chart flashed a major bullish signal, Strategy 
The signal, a golden cross, occurs when a security’s 50-day average price rises above its 200-day average. Some traders read the transition as a decisive bullish shift in momentum that can lead to a prolonged rally.
For MSTR, which holds $69.81 billion in bitcoin, the cross could happen as soon as Monday. Since the company began buying the largest cryptocurrency for its balance sheet in August 2020, the stock has had two such crosses, and huge rallies followed both.
The first happened on Sept. 15, 2020, with the stock at about $15.57. MSTR climbed to $127.29 by February 2021, a gain of 717%. A death cross, the opposite of golden cross, followed in January 2022. By then, the stock was at $46.83, still triple the value on the day the bullish signal first appeared.
The second came on March 2, 2023, at $25.29. The shares peaked at $473.83 in November 2024, up 1,774%. When the death cross arrived in October 2025, MSTR was at $328.40, still 1,199% higher.
It’s worth keeping in mind that the signal isn’t especially reliable. In MSTR’s case, since 1999, the shares have registered 19 golden crosses. On 11 occasions, the stock was higher three months later, and after only 10 was it higher 12 months later, according to data analyzed by CoinDesk.
That’s a record of 50% accuracy. The median 12-month return was just 3.3%, and the two worst crosses, in 2001 and 2007, were followed by a 61% loss.
Since bitcoin confirmed its golden cross on Sept. 8, it has risen by nearly 5% to $82,000, extending the rally from July lows under $60,000. The price hit a high of over $87,000 early this month.
It remains to be seen if MSTR follows bitcoin’s lead. Stay alert!

The 50-day average looks set to cross above its longer-term counterpart, confirming a golden cross. This follows a trendline breakout, another bullish development, and suggests potential for further price gains.

Although large rallies followed Strategy's two examples since it began buying bitcoin, CoinDesk's longer historical review found the signal was followed by a higher share price a year later only about half the time.

title: Live updates: Bitcoin edges higher as U.S. stocks rebound early Monday
article_text:

Bitcoin treasury company Strive continued to add large numbers of BTC to its balance sheet, while far larger peer Strategy acquired only a small amount.
Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor is coming under some social media heat for the company’s continued buybacks of its high-yielding preferred stock STRC at just modest discounts to $100 par value.
The company this morning announced the repurchase of $193 million of STRC, bringing total buybacks to nearly $2 billion. Strategy also announced an increase in the authorized buyback amount to $3 billion from $2 billion.
Recall that the buyback program started this past summer following STRC plunging nearly all the way to $70, putting in question the future of the security. In recent weeks, though, STRC has traded mostly above $98, prompting some to wonder if Strategy’s money might not be better spent on buying more bitcoin at what may (or may not) be close to bear market lows, rather than repurchasing preferred stock trading at only a very minor discount.
And others are curious that the fast pace of buybacks (Strategy has less than $9 billion of STRC issued), combined with a 12% dividend yield, hasn’t been enough to fully return STRC to $100.
“You don’t build a market worth trillions without investing billions,” said Saylor on Monday, in response to some of that criticism.
US midterm elections unlikely to drive crypto prices, Schwab says
The upcoming U.S. midterm elections may have less impact on crypto prices than investors expect, according to Jim Ferraioli, head of crypto research at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.
Schwab found little evidence that rising odds of Democrats taking control of Congress have consistently weighed on crypto returns, even when prediction market trading volumes were high.
While election headlines could trigger short-term volatility, Ferraioli said congressional control has explained little of crypto's recent price movements.
Bipartisan support for crypto legislation and the possibility of continued regulatory progress also suggest that a divided Congress would not necessarily hurt the market.
Troubled neocloud CoreWeave (CRWV) — despite a general risk-on attitude on Monday and an upgrade to buy at Goldman Sachs — has been unable to hold onto early gains.
The stock minutes ago sank below $60 to a new 52-week low after earlier rising to $66.
Yields back on the rise as last week's market panic abates
A shaky start for U.S. stocks has resolved to the upside in late-morning trading, with the Nasdaq sitting at a session high, up 1.8%. The S&P 500 is also at its high for the day, up 0.9%.
Gains are being led by the roughed-up AI space, with defensive sectors like healthcare and consumer staples — which were positive last week — posting modest losses.
Despite two of the uglier inflation reports in recent memory, the U.S. bond market surged last week as the tumble in equities prompted investors to put money into “safe” fixed income.
The panic having subsided for the moment, interest rates are back on the rise. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is up 3.3 basis points to 5.133% after having nearly fallen through 5% at one point last week. Rate hike odds for next week’s Fed meeting have risen to 18% after having dropped to as low as 12% last week.
'Davos in the desert' faces questions after attacks in Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabian organizers are mulling the postponement of the annual Future Investment Initiative — often dubbed “Davos in the desert” — after upped attacks against Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Houthis, reported the FT.
Also under discussion, instead of postponement, would be holding the event virtually, the story added.
Among the scheduled speakers are BlackRock’s Larry Fink and JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon.
Homebuilder sentiment tumbles to weakest since 2012
Surging interest rates appear to be forcing another leg down in the housing industry.
The NAHB Housing Market Index for newly built homes fell to 29 this month from an already weak 32 in September. Economist forecasts had been for the gauge to remain steady at 32.
The NAHB is a diffusion index, meaning a reading above 50 suggests more confidence; below 50, the opposite.
Current sales conditions fell two points in October to 33. Sales expectations in the next six months slid five points to 32. Buyer traffic fell five points to 18.
The survey found 43% of builders cutting prices in October, the highest rate in the 2020-2026 period.
Bitcoin trading at $82,000 as stocks open with tenuous gains
Roughly 30 minutes into the U.S. trading day, tech stocks are bouncing from last week’s carnage, but the gains are a bit more modest than futures trading suggested.
The Nasdaq is ahead 0.85%, with roughed-up AI-related favorites like Micron, Intel, SanDisk, and AMD posting gains in the 4%-7% range.
The S&P 500 is higher by 0.4%, and the DJIA is down 0.25%.
After touching $83,000 overnight, bitcoin has drifted back down to $82,000, up 0.8% over the past 24 hours. Ether, solana, and XRP are also slightly higher.
Metaplanet moves closer to U.S. bitcoin treasury platform as shareholders approve Superplanet deal
Super League shareholders have approved Metaplanet’s proposed takeover, according to Metaplanet CEO, Simon Gerovich, which paves the way for the companys rebrand to Superplanet (SUPA), a U.S.-listed bitcoin treasury platform.
At closing, Metaplanet will contribute 2,100 BTC out of its 44,000 BTC and $2.5 million for approximately 93.7% ownership, with its shares locked up for five years.
Superplanet plans to grow bitcoin per share primarily through non-convertible perpetual preferred stock, expanding Metaplanet’s access to U.S. capital markets.
Strategy purchased 267 bitcoin last week, while Strive added 1,223
Michael Saylor’s Strategy MSTR$130.49·Market Closed acquired a modest 267 bitcoin last week, bringing total holdings to 848,517 coins. The company also bought back another $193 million of its high-yielding preferred stock STRC and boosted the size of that repurchase program to $3 billion from $2 billion.
STRC fell back to $97.72 during last week’s market-wide selloff, likely indicating that Saylor and team will continue buying back shares rather than issuing them to acquire more bitcoin.
The company will have another $600 million in buying power later this week when the IPO proceeds from its SATA preferred stock offering hit its bank account.
Strive’s original high-yielding preferred stock SATA was also caught up in the market panic last week, falling all the way back to $96.83. It had previously spent several weeks trading at or above par value ($100), allowing the company to use it as a funding mechanism to buy more bitcoin.
Cboe’s VIX index, also known as Wall Street’s fear gauge, is down 5% as of this writing.
The index, representing the market’s expectations for the degree of price swings in the S&P 500 over the next four weeks, is hovering just below 19. It surged by over 20% to nearly 20 on Friday as AI stocks tanked.
French bond spread on the rise after weekend riots
The U.S. equity market appears poised for a strong rebound on Monday, and Treasury rates are slipping, but that’s not the case in Europe.
Leading a 1.3% decline in the Euro Stoxx 50 is France’s CAC 40, lower by 1.65% following ugly-looking rioting in that country over the weekend.
Bond yields are moving higher as well; the French 10-year OAT yield is up 11 basis points to 4.89%, while the German 10-year Bund yield gains just 3.5% basis points to 3.44%. That puts the 10-year spread between the two to 145 basis points, the highest level in two weeks.
Bitcoin’s weekend bounce is still just a rebound, FxPro says, as bulls lean on October seasonality
Dip buyers defended bitcoin’s 50-day moving average again over the weekend, lifting it 1.4% to about $82,800 on Monday, but FxPro’s chief market analyst Alex Kuptsikevich is calling it a rebound for now.
The 50-day moving average, bitcoin’s average closing price over the past 50 days, sits near $81,000 and has caught every dip since last Tuesday. Holding it keeps the medium-term trend intact. Breaking higher takes more than that.
“This rise is better described as a rebound than a resumption of upward momentum,” Kuptsikevich said in an email to CoinDesk.
He pointed to last summer as a guide, when bitcoin chopped around similar levels for more than a month back then, and only a sharp surge on Aug. 19 kicked off the rally that followed.
Bulls are leaning on the calendar. Traditional markets often put in a local bottom toward the end of October, Kuptsikevich said, and crypto investors are betting that pattern helps them claw back last week’s losses.
'Irrational despair': Neolcouds rising early Monday after last week's plunge
“Irrational despair,” goes the title of a note from StoneX’s Mark Palmer on Galaxy Digital GLXY$15.98·Market Closed, one of the names swept up in the panic over AI data center stocks over the past couple of weeks.
The market is valuing GLXY as if CoreWeave (CRWV) — Galaxy’s tenant at its Helios data center — has already failed and Galaxy could find no other tenants, argued Palmer.
He reiterated his buy rating and $57 price target on GLXY. GLXY is higher by 3% pre-market to $16.80 following last week’s 20% decline.
Goldman Sachs is boosting the mood as well, upgrading CoreWeave to buy from neutral.
Elon Musk to give away SpaceX shares to American children
“Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX SPCX$134.71·Market Closed shares to every kid in America,” tweeted Elon Musk early Monday morning. “This will be the first of many.”
The company reports its third-quarter results after the close on Thursday.
Oil reverses early drop as U.S. issues security alerts across Middle East nations
Oil prices have bounced from Asian session lows on fears of a fresh escalation in Middle East geopolitical tensions.
WTI futures have recovered to $98.55, down just 0.5% on the day, after hitting a low of $96.72 during Asian hours. Bitcoin BTC$77,261.24 and ether ETH$2,242.84 have erased their early gains.
A few hours ago, the U.S. reportedly issued warnings across 12 locations in the Middle East, warning it citizens of potential flight cancellations and airspace closures. This has triggered fears of fresh U.S. strikes on Iran and continued disruption of oil flow through the pivotal Strait of Hormuz.
Bitcoin pokes above $83,000 for a moment as tech futures snap a weeklong skid
Bitcoin climbed from an overnight low near $80,700 to just above $83,000 early Monday, then slipped back to about $82,400 within half an hour. Sellers were waiting for the move.
It was a quick turn. Bitcoin is up 0.3% over 24 hours, and $83,000 is still about $1,000 short of the ceiling that turned it back twice last week, near $84,000 on Oct. 13 and again on Oct. 14.
The bounce tracked a rebound in tech. Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 1.1%, snapping a weeklong 5.5% selloff, and S&P 500 futures rose 0.5%. An ETF tracking chipmakers jumped 3% before the U.S. open, on course for its first gain in 10 sessions. This week’s earnings will put the AI trade under the spotlight again.
Europe was weaker. The Stoxx 600 fell 0.8% after a weekend of protests in France, French bonds led a selloff in European debt, and the euro was the worst performer among major currencies. The dollar was flat, and Brent crude slipped from a five-month high.

title: Bitcoin mining offshoot Nscale loses Microsoft AI deal as power delay stretches into 2030s
article_text:
Bitcoin mining offshoot Nscale loses Microsoft AI deal as power delay stretches into 2030s. Bitcoin mining offshoot Nscale loses Microsoft AI deal as power delay stretches into 2030s
The Nvidia-backed company planned to deliver 23,000 AI chips in the U.K. next year, but its grid connection may not be ready until the 2030s.
- Microsoft abandoned a planned Nscale AI data center in the U.K. after the local grid operator said sufficient power might not be available until the early-to-mid 2030s.
- The facility was expected to supply 50 megawatts of computing capacity to Microsoft’s Azure cloud by early 2027, using 23,040 Nvidia chips.
- The setback highlights the power and financing challenges facing bitcoin miners expanding into AI infrastructure, as U.K. data center grid-connection requests total about 73 gigawatts.
Technology giant Microsoft 
The site in Loughton, Essex, about 6 miles northeast of London, was meant to house 23,040 Nvidia chips and supply 50 megawatts of computing to Microsoft’s Azure cloud by early 2027, according to the Guardian, which followed initial reporting by the Financial Times. UK Power Networks, which runs the local grid, told Nscale there may not be enough capacity until the early-to-mid 2030s.
Nscale announced the project last year alongside Microsoft, Nvidia 
Nscale grew out of Arkon Energy, which built sites for bitcoin mining. Its founder, Josh Payne, took that experience in locking down land and power and turned it into a business selling computing to AI companies. Much of the listed mining industry is now running that playbook.
When CoinDesk looked at the industry shift in March, public miners had announced more than $70 billion in AI and high-performance computing contracts. They had also cut their combined bitcoin holdings by more than 15,000 BTC from their peaks, partly by selling coins to pay for the buildout.
Mining was already getting squeezed then. The report put the average listed miner’s cash cost to produce one bitcoin near $80,000 in the fourth quarter of 2025, and bitcoin was trading around $70,000 by March.
AI contracts pay steadily for years, but the sites are far more expensive to build. Estimates suggest an AI-ready facility runs $8 million to $15 million per megawatt, compared with roughly $700,000 to $1 million for bitcoin mining, and AI customers expect the servers to stay up around the clock.
The money also takes time to show up. In its latest mining report, fund manager CoinShares counted more than 4 gigawatts of AI capacity under contract across the miners it tracks, with only about 550 megawatts actually billing customers. Contract backlogs topped $100 billion, while annualized AI revenue stood at just over $1 billion.
Unless Nscale finds its own power or gets the grid to move a lot faster, the site it just cleared could sit idle for years.
Meanwhile, Britain’s grid queue is long. Energy regulator Ofgem says data center projects have requested connections totaling about 73 gigawatts of demand. It is weighing tougher rules because some applicants may never build, which holds up projects that are ready to go.

UPDATE (Oct. 19, 11:23 UTC): Adds site’s location relative to London in second paragraph.
reference_summary: Microsoft abandoned a planned Nscale artificial-intelligence data center in the U.K. after the local grid operator said enough electricity might not be available until the early-to-mid 2030s. The site was supposed to supply Microsoft's Azure service with 23,040 Nvidia chips and 50 megawatts of computing capacity by early 2027. Nscale grew out of a bitcoin-mining business, and the setback highlights the power and funding challenges facing mining companies expanding into AI.

title: U.S. CFTC rebuffs CME legal stance in consequential fight over perpetual futures
article_text:
U.S. CFTC rebuffs CME legal stance in consequential fight over perpetual futures. U.S. CFTC rebuffs CME legal stance in consequential fight over perpetual futures
The future of perps in the U.S. may be at stake as the CFTC argues that CME hasn't shown the new policy is hurting it after the agency OK'd its first bitcoin perp.
- The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission is seeking to cast doubt on CME Group's legal challenge to its new perps policy.
- The CFTC filed a brief in court arguing that the derivatives giant hasn't shown it's being harmed by the government's new push into perpetual futures, and without harm, it doesn't have legal standing.
The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission threw open the doors for perpetual futures in the U.S. in May, approving the first bitcoin perp from Kalshi and suggesting that it was open for business on ensuring a domestic surge in such contracts. But the CME Group objected in court, and the CFTC has responded in court that the derivatives giant has no right to get in the way.
"Allegations of increased competition, without any plausible inference of an imminent financial injury," don't give CME the legal standing to challenge the CFTC's actions, the agency said in a brief filed on Friday, noting that volume in crypto futures at the CME has actually risen since its policy shift.
Perp contracts had soared overseas, becoming a major form of transaction in crypto derivatives, and the CFTC's move sought to clarify how the market could get rolling in the U.S. The agency — in response to President Donald Trump's aggressive crypto agenda that included bringing perps into domestic trading — said it'll regulate the products on a case-by-case basis as futures.
Perps allow traders to speculate on the future price of an asset with a typically leveraged position, and the contracts don't come with a built-in expiration.
But CME, which operates the leading global venues for derivatives trading, has insisted the contracts are not futures, because they have no end date. They're really swaps, the company's argument would have it, which would come with an entirely different regulatory approach. Spokespeople for CME didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the CFTC's latest filing.
The CFTC first asked a federal judge to dismiss CME's case last month, and this latest filing details its argument against the company's legal standing.
"CME must plausibly allege an actual or imminent increase in competition," the CFTC argued. "CME has not even done that."
The agency argued that CME has been telling investors that it hasn't heard of a demand for perps and that they aren't substitutes for the futures it's offering.
"CME cannot have it one way with the court and another way with the investing public on earnings calls," the CFTC contended in its brief.
Jaret Seiberg, a policy analyst at TD Cowen, argued in a Monday client note that CME may still have the edge, in both its standing as a competitor and its argument that perps may be appropriately treated as swaps. However, the clock is ticking on the new market.
"What increasingly concerns us is the growth in perps while the litigation is playing out," Seiberg wrote. "If this growth continues, it could create complications in trying to unwind this market if the CME prevails in the lawsuit."
Read More: Inside the CME and CFTC’s battle over onchain perpetual futures
reference_summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission asked a court to reject CME Group's challenge to its policy allowing perpetual futures, contracts that let traders bet on prices without an expiry date. The regulator argues CME has not shown actual or imminent financial harm that would give it the right to sue. CME says the contracts should be treated as a different financial product under different rules, leaving their U.S. regulation in dispute.

title: Zerohash rolls out a new tool to move crypto without copying wallet addresses
article_text:
Zerohash rolls out a new tool to move crypto without copying wallet addresses. Zerohash rolls out a new tool to move crypto without copying wallet addresses
The launch comes as Zerohash bids for a federal trust charter.
- Users can approve transfers without copying wallet addresses or choosing a blockchain network.
- Zerohash says AUTH supports more than 600 connections, with 4 of them being exchange or brokerage accounts and the rest being wallets.
Zerohash launched AUTH, a service that lets users move crypto between linked accounts without copying wallet addresses or choosing a blockchain network, simplifying digital asset transactions.
The crypto services firm announced the tool, which lets users link exchange accounts or self-custody wallets at the Money20/20 conference in Las Vegas.
“Onchain rails scale when users stop thinking about the underlying technology. Usability, trust and control is the inflection point for mass adoption,” said Ryan Beaudry, general manager of AUTH. Beaudry, who was previously executive vice president of global product and operations for open finance at Mastercard, will be the general manager of AUTH, according to a statement.
AUTH supports crypto, stablecoins and blockchain-based securities like stock tokens. Zerohash said the service supports more than 600 connections, including Coinbase, Robinhood, Gemini, MetaMask and Phantom. Zerohash’s developer documentation listed support for 639 wallets and four exchange or brokerage accounts. Coinbase, Robinhood and Gemini are live, while Kraken is in beta.
The launch comes as Zerohash seeks to expand its regulatory standing. In July, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency returned the firm’s application for a national trust bank charter, a step the agency takes when it considers a filing materially deficient. The firm called the return an administrative process and refiled a narrower application on Aug. 18. The application is still pending.
The goal of this new product is to reduce the steps required to move funds, the firm said.
To make a transaction, users pick an account or wallet inside an app that offers AUTH, sign in and approve the move. The service handles routing and settlement, while each app sets which assets, accounts and transfer types it allows.
Alex LaPrade, CEO of a popular non-custodial Ethereum and multi-chain crypto wallet, said that transfers to wallets have previously involved repeated address checks and test payments, which were “one of the biggest points of friction” that AUTH is aiming to simplify.
Zerohash, founded in 2017, has a global regulatory footprint across the EU, Latin America, Bermuda, and the U.S., and operates regulated entities in 51 U.S. jurisdictions, according to its website. The Chicago-based company was in acquisition talks with Mastercard, which fell through earlier this year. At the time, Zerohash was reportedly in talks to raise $250 million at a $1.5 billion valuation.
Companies connect to zerohash through APIs and developer tools, and the firm handles custody, compliance, liquidity, settlement, and blockchain connectivity. The firm already provides crypto infrastructure for firms, including Morgan Stanley’s E*Trade.
reference_summary: Zerohash launched AUTH, a service that lets users transfer cryptocurrency between linked accounts by signing in and approving the move, without copying wallet addresses or choosing a network. The company says it supports more than 600 wallet, exchange and brokerage connections, including Coinbase, Robinhood, MetaMask and Phantom. Each app offering AUTH decides which assets, accounts and types of transfer it allows.

title: Bitcoin extends bounce above $82,000 as stocks rebound, DeFi tokens lead altcoin gains
article_text:
Bitcoin extends bounce above $82,000 as stocks rebound, DeFi tokens lead altcoin gains. Bitcoin traded around $82,500, up about 0.4% since midnight UTC, extending a rebound from Sunday’s dip to roughly $80,700.
The CoinDesk 80 gained 0.9%, triple the CoinDesk 5’s 0.e5% rise, with all six members of the DeFi index higher and arbitrum adding 6.7%.
Nasdaq 100 futures rose more than 1% and Asian stocks advanced after China’s third-quarter GDP growth beat expectations and oil prices eased.
Bitcoin BTC$77,789.54 is trading around $82,500, up around 0.5% since midnight UTC, extending a bounce from Sunday’s dip to roughly $80,700 and comfortably above Thursday’s brief break below $80,000.
Altcoins outpaced the largest cryptocurrency, with ether ETH$2,265.69 adding 0.75% to near $2,430 and the CoinDesk 80 (CD80) gaining 0.9%, triple the 0.35% rise in the bitcoin-heavy CoinDesk 5 (CD5). DeFi led the CoinDesk benchmarks with a 0.81% gain, with all six members of the DFX sector index higher.
The rebound follows a rough week for U.S. tech. The Nasdaq fell 4.5% in its worst weekly decline since June as worries over AI spending and debt hit stocks such as CoreWeave (CRWV), which fell 25%. On Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures advanced more than 1% alongside gains in Asian stocks after China’s third-quarter GDP growth of 4.5% beat expectations and oil prices eased, with earnings from Meta Platforms META$615.06·Market Closed and Tesla TSLA$399.82·Market Closed due this week.
Derivatives positioning
Volume jumps, positioning doesn't: Total 24-hour crypto futures volume rose 51% to $146 billion, while open interest (OI) edged up just 1.25% to $141 billion as traders churned through more contracts without adding much net exposure. Liquidations were $329 million, little changed from a day earlier, and the taker long-short volume ratio is balanced, so neither side is forcing the other out.
Majors rally with more leverage than spot buying: BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP all gained, and their notional OI grew faster than their prices in a sign that fresh capital is entering the contracts. Annualized perpetual funding is positive on all four, so longs are paying to hold. The 24-hour OI-adjusted cumulative volume delta (CVD) is flat to negative, though, meaning aggressive selling at least matched aggressive buying. The gains look position-led, and that makes them more fragile.
DOGE, UNI and crude oil perps see positions unwind: OI fell in all three despite flat-to-negative price action. Traders are closing positions and pulling capital out, not adding to bets on the downside.
ADA's bounce meets bearish positioning: ADA rose almost 1% in 24 hours, yet its annualized perp funding is -8%, the only negative print among the majors. Shorts are paying to stay short, and CVD is negative too. If the bounce continues, that crowded short side could become a source of buying.
Crypto volatility gauges stay calm as the VIX spikes: Bitcoin's and ether's 30-day implied volatility indexes, BVIV and EVIV, still signal calm, even as Wall Street's equivalent, VIX, surged on Friday. VIX history points to a likely normalization on Monday.
Bitcoin put-buyers dominate Deribit: The five most traded options on Deribit over the past 24 hours were all bitcoin puts at strikes below the current market price. Traders use puts to hedge long exposure against spot declines, so some are insuring gains. Ether flows look mixed.
Token talk
Arbitrum ARB$0.1648, an Ethereum layer-2 token, rose 6.7% to about $0.20, with the rally stemming from the Arbitrum Foundation’s Stablecoin Growth Program, announced on Thursday. The program sets aside 2 million ARB for the first 10 teams to hold $10 million in USDG, a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Paxos Digital Singapore. ARB has risen by 16.45% since the announcement.
Pump.fun PUMP$0.004228, the token of the Solana memecoin launchpad, jumped 7.6%, recouping part of a weekend slide that took it to about $0.0039 on Sunday. While there was no news catalyst for the move, 24-hour trading volume doubled to $215 million.
DeFi tokens advanced across the board, with uniswap (UNI) up 3.2% to around $7.42, while lido LDO$0.3334 and ethena (ENA) rose by 2.5% and 1.6% respectively as the sector recovers from last month’s Clarity Act delay and shrinking yields.
Celestia (TIA) gave back 3.9% to about 61 cents after Friday’s 16% jump, while starknet STRK$0.04284 slipped 1.0% to 6 cents. STRK’s market value has fallen about a quarter since Friday morning, according to CoinDesk data.
The larger cryptocurrencies were mostly higher, with solana (SOL) rising 1.6% to about $106, XRP gaining 0.6% and BNB adding 0.36%. Cardano ADA$0.1935 slipped 0.15% and hedera HBAR$0.07223 fell 0.83%.
The “Altcoin Season” index is at 56/100, tumbling from last week’s high of 63/100, the 2026 record.

Arbitrum rose 6.7% after announcing incentives for attracting deposits in the USDG digital dollar. The broader rebound accompanied gains in Asian stocks and Nasdaq-linked contracts after stronger-than-expected Chinese growth and easing oil prices.

title: Tether: Senator's investigation misses positive work that's led to lower Iran volumes
article_text:
Tether: Senator's investigation misses positive work that's led to lower Iran volumes. Tether: Senator's investigation misses positive work that's led to lower Iran volumes
The stablecoin issuer's CEO, Paolo Ardoino, has been defending against accusations that the firm's stablecoins have fueled financial activity in Iran.
- Tether CEO Paulo Ardoino posted on X that his company is often way ahead of government sanctions when it freezes suspicious transactions — a point he contends a recent report from Senate Democrats ignored.
- He said he's confident Tether is "doing the right thing."
Tether is answering back against a report issued last month by Democrats on the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations that had accused the stablecoin firm of providing "a significant financial lifeline within Iran's shadow banking network," with Tether CEO Paulo Ardoino saying Monday that the probe missed the positive work it's doing to observe sanctions.
Senator Richard Blumenthal, the subcommittee's top Democrat, led the effort, which further highlighted Democratic lawmakers' concerns that crypto is used to support illicit finance. But Ardoino contends that Tether freezes suspicious transactions well before entities such as the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control and Israel's National Bureau for Counter Terror Financing formally flag them.
"Senator Blumenthal's 'analysis' of Tether's sanctions report misses that, since 2023, Tether froze on average 4 weeks prior to OFAC & NBCTF official sanction designation and for 99% of the times Tether froze the reported addresses before Chainalysis labelled them," Ardoino wrote in a post on social media site X.
Ardoino went on to argue that the company's actions "led to Iran-linked stablecoin volumes declining by 94%."
Tether's CEO also spoke remotely at a Washington event, DC Fintech Week, and addressed the senator's report there, as well, last Tuesday. He criticized how it was released to the media before his company could review it.
"I believe it's important for the public also to hear our side of the story," he said.
"Our aim is to push out the bad actors from USDT," Ardoino said. "Those bad actors are moving to other means that are outside of the control of the United States, and now outside of our control."
He added that the work "is not finished," but he said he's happy with Tether's role.
"I wake up in the morning and I look at myself in the mirror, and I know that we're doing the right thing," he said.
The Senate report went back a number of years, focusing in part on the period before 2024 in which it said Tether didn't comprehensively freeze flagged wallets. "This absence of deterrence invited abuse: Terrorist organizations such as Hamas shifted from transacting in bitcoin and a mix of cryptocurrencies to promoting USDT," it said.
Since the report, Blumenthal has additionally been probing the relationship between Tether and its U.S. financial partner, Cantor Fitzgerald, which has close ties to the administration of President Donald Trump. Tether also named Bo Hines, Trump's former White House crypto adviser, as the CEO of its U.S. division last fall.
In recent weeks, the odds that Democrats — including Blumenthal — may return to the majority in the Senate have been climbing, according to prediction market Kalshi. If that happens, Blumenthal could have significantly increased powers to investigate crypto matters.
Read More: Tether's $344 million USDT freeze linked to U.S. 'Economic Fury' against Iran regime
reference_summary: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino rejected a Senate Democratic report accusing its USDT digital currency, designed to track the U.S. dollar, of supporting Iran's hidden financial networks. Ardoino said Tether often blocked suspicious wallets before official sanctions and claimed its actions reduced Iran-linked stablecoin activity by 94%. The Senate report said the company had not consistently frozen flagged wallets in earlier years.

title: Bitcoin ETFs just saw their biggest day in a month thanks entirely to BlackRock
article_text:
Bitcoin ETFs just saw their biggest day in a month thanks entirely to BlackRock. Bitcoin ETFs just saw their biggest day in a month thanks entirely to BlackRock
Fidelity's FBTC and Grayscale's GBTC saw outflows of $83.6 million and $54.9 million, respectively.
- U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs added $526.6 million on Monday, led entirely by BlackRock’s IBIT net inflow of $665.2 million.
- Fidelity's FBTC and Grayscale's GBTC saw outflows of $83.6 million and $54.9 million, respectively.
- Ether funds dropped $103.3 million, marking a fourth consecutive session of outflows.
U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds attracted $526.6 million on Monday, the largest daily net inflow in nearly a month, driven entirely by BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT).
IBIT pulled in $665.2 million, its biggest daily inflow since Oct. 7 last year, according to SoSoValue data. Combined, the bitcoin funds last drew more on Sept. 22, when they added $714.7 million.
Fidelity’s FBTC lost $83.6 million, while Grayscale’s GBTC shed $54.9 million in Monday’s trading session, while the remaining funds recorded no net flows, underscoring how concentrated buying was.
The inflow more than erased last week’s $228.5 million of withdrawals, though the funds remain about $90.5 million in the red for October, according to CoinDesk calculations using SoSoValue’s figures.
Ether funds moved in the opposite direction, losing $103.3 million in their fourth consecutive session of outflows. BlackRock’s ETHA accounted for $95.4 million of the withdrawals, according to SoSoValue.
reference_summary: U.S. investment funds that hold bitcoin attracted $526.6 million more than investors withdrew on Monday, their largest daily net inflow in nearly a month, according to SoSoValue. BlackRock's IBIT received $665.2 million, more than offsetting withdrawals from Fidelity's FBTC and Grayscale's GBTC. Funds holding ether lost $103.3 million in their fourth consecutive day of withdrawals.

title: South Korean IPO plunge deepens AI market jitters as brent tops $111
article_text:
South Korean IPO plunge deepens AI market jitters as brent tops $111. South Korean IPO slump adds to AI market jitters as Brent crude tops $111
Elice’s debut slump added to concerns over AI infrastructure valuations, while rising oil prices compounded market uncertainty.
- South Korean data centre Elice closed a third below its IPO price despite retail demand exceeding 400 times the allocation, as the KOSPI fell almost 4%.
- CoreWeave slipped another 3% in pre-market trading.
- Brent crude topped $111 a barrel amid persistent Middle Eastern concerns.
South Korean data centre company Elice’s (0158S0) stock market debut added to nervousness surrounding artificial intelligence investments on Tuesday, as investors further questioned whether spending on infrastructure will deliver sufficient returns.
The Seoul-based neocloud provider closed at 60,500 won ($45.57), down over 30% from its 90,500 won offer price. The IPO raised $151 million at a valuation of roughly $755 million, according to Bloomberg. The slump followed a retail offering oversubscribed more than 400 times.
Pressure has extended into U.S. pre-market trading, where CoreWeave (CRWV) fell another 3%. The neocloud sector faces scrutiny over borrowing costs, high debt levels and the profitability of capital-intensive expansion plans. Technology shares, bitcoin and gold were also lower on Tuesday morning.
Elice’s weak debut accompanied another sell-off in South Korean equities. The KOSPI dropped almost 4% to finish at 5,552, with Samsung Electronics falling around 3% and SK Hynix losing roughly 4%.
Meanwhile, Brent crude topped $111 a barrel, reaching its highest level since May, while WTI traded around $100. Brent’s roughly $11 premium reflected persistent concerns about Middle Eastern supply disruptions and shipping risks.
reference_summary: South Korean AI data center company Elice fell more than 30% below its offer price on its first day of stock trading, despite heavy demand before the listing. South Korea's KOSPI stock index dropped almost 4%, and CoreWeave shares also fell before U.S. markets opened as investors questioned AI spending and profitability. Brent oil exceeded $111 a barrel amid concerns over Middle Eastern supply disruptions.

title: Live updates: Market jitters persist as the AI selloff deepens
article_text:
Live updates: Market jitters persist as the AI selloff deepens. Elon Musk’s SpaceX SPCX$134.71·Market Closed reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion (up 161% year-over-year), topping estimates for $12.87 billion.
Adjusted EBITDA of $8.81 billion was ahead of forecasts for $6.59 billion. Net income of $4.4 billion topped forecasts for $1.88 billion.
Capital expenditures for the quarter were $19.59 billion, about in line with estimates for $19.6 billion.
Cash and cash equivalents at quarter’s end were $51.29 billion, well shy of forecasts for $91.2 billion. Bitcoin on the balance sheet was valued at $1.57 billion.
Shares are flat in after-hours trading at $148, roughly a $2 trillion valuation.
Anthropic prospectus shows fast growth, heavy spend: WSJ
AI giant Anthropic had revenue of about $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.1 billioin a year earlier, according to the WSJ, which viewed a draft of the company’s S-1 as it preps for an IPO.
Spending on compute capacity grew fast as well, hitting $9 billion in the first half, up from $2.3 billion in the same period in 2025. Further, Anthropic is contracted to spend around $450 billion on agreements currently in place over the next 7 to 10 years.
The company booked a net loss of more than $80 billion in the first half of this year, up from $13 billion a year earlier.
Amazon storing billions in Nvidia hardware in warehouses
It turns out that data center power generation and buildouts are lagging well behind hardware in the AI race.
According to Business Insider, Amazon AMZN$240.45·Market Closed is buying GPUs so far in advance that it is storing billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia hardware in warehouses because it’s got no place to plug them in.
The story said that Amazon expects to take delivery of $3 billion worth of GPUs per month for the foreseeable future.
The half-life of these Iran peace deal reports can be measured in minutes.
Oil has gained back about $2 of its earlier loss on a report of a denial of an earlier report of major progress on a compromise to end the war in Iran.
WTI crude is now at $97.60 per barrel, down just 1% on the day.
The Nasdaq has returned to flat on the session, and bitcoin has retreated about 1% from its session high, now trading back to $82,300.
Bitcoin sheds overnight losses, rising back to $83,000
Down alongside stocks early, bitcoin BTC$77,903.57 has quickly risen back to $83,000 as U.S. stocks also turn positive.
Perhaps helping is a reversal in oil prices. WTI crude oil had jumped above $101 per barrel at one point overnight, but is now modestly lower on the session at $98.15.
U.S. bond yields are also lower, the 10-year Treasury down 3.7 basis points at 5.10%.
Pending home sales miss by a mile in latest sign of interest rate bite
U.S. pending home sales tumbled 7.3% in September, according to the NAR. That was far worse than forecasts for just a 0.5% slump.
On a year-over-year basis, pending home sales fell 11.3%. The actual read of 66.0 is the weakest print in the 25-year history of the pending home sales gauge.
“Market conditions weakened in September due to fast-rising mortgage rates,” said the NAR’s Lawrence Yun. “Although job growth and income gains can support home purchases, housing affordability is more affected by changes in mortgage rates.”
A government report earlier this morning showed a steep decline in new home sales, and a report yesterday from the NAHB showed builder confidence falling to a 14-year low.
The economic pressure on Iran is intensifying, said U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in a Tuesday morning appearance. The currency has collapsed, and panic is beginning to spread. The country’s economy, he said, “will go non-linear at some point.”
As for the U.S., Bessent contended that, aside from the energy price spike, most things are going well.
Of that energy spike, oil prices have fallen about $2 per barrel from their overnight highs but remain elevated, with WTI crude for December delivery at $98.40 per barrel.
More evidence that higher interest rates are biting:
Housing starts in September fell 5.2% to a seasonally adjusted annualized rate of 1.221 million, according to just-released government data. That’s well below economist forecasts of 1.3 million. August starts were 1.288 million.
Building permits fell to 1.4 million from 1.403 million, and slightly above forecasts for 1.39 million.
Just yesterday, the NAHB reported that homebuilder confidence tumbled to its weakest level since 2012.
French bond spreads are blowing out anew on Tuesday, with that country’s 10-year OAT yield rising 3.4 basis points to 4.956% and the German 10-year Bund yield sliding 3 basis points to 3.43%.
This brings the spread between the two core EMU members back to about a cycle high of 153 basis points, the widest level since the continent’s debt crisis in 2011.
ECB member Olli Rehn, testifying Tuesday in Finland’s parliament, conceded that French bond spreads have widened “somewhat.”
“All euro-area countries must bring their public deficits under control and thereby ensure their debt sustainability,” said Rehn. “This goes just as much for France as it does for Finland.”
France’s CAC 40 is leading European stocks lower, down 0.8% today, and off about 12% since peaking two months ago.
Bitget agrees to buy licensed Thai crypto exchange in Southeast Asia push
Crypto exchange Bitget said it plans to acquire GMO-Z, a licensed cryptocurrency exchange and brokerage based in Bangkok, for an undisclosed amount as it expands in Southeast Asia.
The deal would take place through BTGT Management, a company in which Bitget holds an interest.
GMO Internet, its subsidiary GMO-Z and other shareholders would transfer their entire holdings in the exchange to BTGT Management or its designated entity at completion.
Bitget plans to introduce its trading platform to Thai users once the acquisition closes. The transaction is subject to regulatory approval and other conditions.
Switzerland’s financial regulator, FINMA, said it approved a bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) for the first time.
FINMA did not disclose the issuer of the ETF.
Switzerland was the first jurisdiction to approve cryptocurrency exchange-traded products (ETPs). Regulation preventing ETFs from holding only a single asset meant such funds could not be defined as such and so were listed under the umbrella “ETP” designation.
FINMA has now approved an exemption to allow ETFs holding only bitcoin reflecting its “long trading history and particularly high trading volume compared with other cryptocurrencies.”
Market jitters persist as the AI selloff deepens. South Korea’s KOSPI fell almost 4%, accompanied by one of the weakest IPO debuts in the country’s history, with data centre company Elice tumbling around 30%.
The weakness carried into U.S. pre-market trading, with CoreWeave (CRWV) down 4%, Cipher Digital CIFR$7.2870·Market Closed falling 2% and IREN IREN$23.97·Market Closed losing 3%. The Invesco QQQ ETF also traded lower, reflecting broader pressure on technology stocks.

Long-dated U.S. Treasuries appear to be attracting defensive flows, with the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) rising 0.5%.
reference_summary: Markets remained unsettled as concerns about artificial-intelligence spending pushed South Korea's KOSPI stock index down almost 4%, while data center company Elice fell about 30% on its market debut. Bitcoin initially held above $81,000, recovered to $83,000 as U.S. stocks turned positive, then slipped back to about $82,300. Bitcoin slipped 0.5% to around $81,400 even after the biggest daily spot ETF inflow in nearly a month as South Korea's Kospi index fell 3.7% on AI worries.
Bitcoin slipped to around $81,400, down 0.5% since midnight UTC, even after U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs drew $526.6 million on Monday, their largest daily inflow in nearly a month.
South Korea’s Kospi fell 3.73% to its lowest close since April 7 as SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics declined, with renewed AI spending worries weighing on chipmakers’ shares.
Options traders are seeking downside protection, with Deribit puts outtrading calls by more than two to one and a bearish skew across expiries. CoinDesk’s DeFi index fell 1.2%.
Bitcoin BTC$77,766.68 slipped to around $81,400 on Tuesday, down 0.5% since midnight UTC, even after U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds attracted $526.6 million on Monday, their largest daily inflow in nearly a month.
Asian stocks set the tone, with South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index falling 3.73% to its lowest close since April 7 as SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics declined with renewed worries over AI spending weighing on chipmakers’ shares. Nasdaq 100 futures fell 0.31%.
Altcoin losses were broadly in line with bitcoin. Ether ETH$2,264.55 fell 0.9% to near $2,385 and the CoinDesk 80 (CD80) lost 0.34%, compared with a 0.33% drop for the bitcoin-heavy CoinDesk 5 (CD5). DeFi gave back Monday’s lead, with the sector index (DFX) dropping 1.2%, the weakest of the CoinDesk benchmarks.
Brent crude is near $110 a barrel as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keep supply risks in view. Roughly 70 S&P 500 companies report earnings this week, with General Motors before the bell and United Airlines after the close.
Derivatives positioning
Bitcoin open interest on Coinalyze fell to $27.4 billion, down 0.6% over 24 hours, while the aggregated funding rate was roughly 8.8% annualized. Ether’s funding of about 3.9% annualized suggests a bullish bias among traders.
Longs hold around 55% of bitcoin positions, Coinalyze data shows, with a long/short ratio of 1.24. Binance’s top traders show a similar tilt, with a BTC-USDT position ratio of 1.78 on CoinGlass.
Puts outtraded calls by more than two to one on Deribit over 24 hours, with the Oct. 30 $80,000 put the busiest contract. Out-of-the-money puts also cost more than equivalent calls, by 2.5 to 4 volatility points across expiries, a bearish skew that shows traders paying for downside protection even as open interest leans toward calls at $90,000-$100,000 for Oct. 30.
CoinGlass shows $155.1 million of liquidations over 24 hours, down 54.7% from the previous day, with longs about 69% of the total on CoinMarketCap’s tally. Bitcoin and ether each saw around $30 million on Coinalyze, together about half of the $120.6 million it tracked.
Token talk
Celestia (TIA) rose 2.2% to around 63 cents, the biggest gainer on the CoinDesk 100 Index (CD100), adding to a gain of about 42% over the month. The run has coincided with Celestia’s Oct. 1 benchmark showing its Fibre scaling system averaging 3.07 terabits per second. At the same time, options exchange Derive chose Celestia for data availability in its V3 release. The next test is an unlock of 5.58 million TIA on Oct. 31, according to Tokenomist.
Sandbox SAND$0.04652 led the CD100 lower with a 4.5% drop to about 6 cents, giving back part of a gain of about 30% over the month. That rally began after South Korean crypto exchanges Upbit, Bithumb and Coinone lifted trading cautions imposed in August following a bridge exploit.
Layer-2 tokens were among the weakest, with arbitrum ARB$0.1647 falling 3.6% and starknet STRK$0.04284 dropping 3.2%. Starknet remains up about 29% over the month after surging on Oct. 9 and 10, when the network said it was considering becoming a standalone quantum-resistant layer-1 by 2027.
DeFi tokens handed back more of Monday’s rally, with uniswap (UNI) losing 2.3% to about $7.14 and morpho MORPHO$2.3212 down 2.5%. UNI has slumped about 20% over the month even though its fee switch lifted protocol revenue to $14.81 million in September, its strongest month since it began retaining fees, according to Token Terminal.
Ethena (ENA) fell 1.9%, extending a decline of about 30% over the month from a late-September peak near 29 cents. USDe supply of about $4.7 billion, down from a peak near $15 billion, is still well short of the $7.5 billion level at which ENA buybacks would switch on.
reference_summary: Bitcoin slipped 0.5% to around $81,400 as South Korea's KOSPI stock index fell 3.73% amid renewed concerns about spending on artificial intelligence. The decline came despite U.S. bitcoin investment funds attracting $526.6 million the previous day, their largest daily inflow in nearly a month. Trading on Deribit in options protecting against price falls was more than twice as high as trading in options benefiting from price rises.

“Broader equity deleveraging dynamics could transmit to cryptocurrency markets and potentially threaten the $80,000 support level if sustained,” the analsysts wrote.
